input.title: Move LH-11 from TP-1250-02 to TP-1310-04 to cover the failed LH-07

options.description: No reaction. TP-1310-04 (8.4 g/t) has no loader from 09:18 to 17:00 (repair high case 17:30, after the window).
Hold and resume when LH-07 is back at the likely time of 14:30 (PR-0001). TP-1310-04 loses 09:18 to 14:30. The low case of 13:30 loses 4.2 h, 126 t, 34.0 oz. The high case is the same as do_nothing.

Move LH-11 from TP-1250-02 (4.1 g/t, phase carguio, lowest grade among loading-only stopes) to TP-1310-04. Leave 09:45 and arrive 10:45 (1 h, different level). Loss at TP-1310-04 from 09:18 to 10:45 is 43.5 t, 11.75 oz. TP-1250-02 loses 09:45 to 17:00, 145 t, 19.11 oz.

input.calculation: Oz = t x g/t / 31.1035. Productive window 07:00-17:00 = 10 h. Rates: TP-1310-04 is 300 t / 10 h = 30 t/h at 8.4 g/t. TP-1250-02 is 200 t / 10 h = 20 t/h at 4.1 g/t. LOADER-BACKUP-01: cover from the lowest-grade stope. LOADER-BACKUP-02: only stopes in phase 'carguio' can give up a loader. That excludes DF-1310-05, TP-1220-01, TP-1280-02 and TP-1310-07, which are in combined cycles. Among the eligible carguio stopes the grades are 4.1 (TP-1250-02), 5.5 (TP-1280-06), 5.8 (TP-1250-08), 6.0 (TP-1310-11), 6.5 (TP-1340-09), 7.2 (TP-1340-03) and 7.6 (TP-1340-06). The lowest is TP-1250-02 with LH-11, so the rules point to it, and it also gives the best net oz. MOVE-TIME-01: 1250 to 1310 is a different level, so the move takes 1 h. 1) do_nothing: 09:18 to 17:00 is 7.7 h, 231 t x 8.4 / 31.1035 = 62.39 oz. 2) wait_for_repair: 09:18 to 14:30 is 5.2 h, 156 t, 42.13 oz. 3) reassign: the leave time of 09:45 is my assumption, about 15 min after the snapshot. Arrival is 10:45. Loss at 1310-04 is 1.45 h x 30 = 43.5 t, 11.75 oz. Protected at 1310-04 is 10:45 to 17:00 = 6.25 h x 30 = 187.5 t, 187.5 x 8.4 / 31.1035 = 50.64 oz. Lost at 1250-02 is 09:45 to 17:00 = 7.25 h x 20 = 145 t, 145 x 4.1 / 31.1035 = 19.11 oz. Net protected is 50.64 - 19.11 = 31.53 oz. Total at risk is 188.5 t and 30.86 oz, against 42.13 oz for waiting and 62.39 oz for doing nothing. The calculation assumes LH-11 stays at 1310-04 to the end of the shift. If LH-07 returns around 14:30, LH-11 could go back to 1250-02 (1 h move). That would recover about 1.5 h x 20 t/h = 30 t, 3.9 oz, but it is not counted here. The repair estimate comes from PR-0001, which is only a crew guess from EV-0001.

The pump diagnosis is unconfirmed. The crew at 1310-04 should confirm it after inspection, and the maintenance warehouse should confirm the pump spare is in stock.
LH-11 operator and ramp availability, and whether TP-1250-02 has any constraint on stopping loading. Ask the shift supervisor (jefe de guardia).

content.text:
I submitted proposal PR-0002 for approval. It moves LH-11 from TP-1250-02 to TP-1310-04 to cover the failed LH-07, starting by 09:45. The move takes 1 h, so LH-11 arrives at 10:45.

- **Why LH-11:** TP-1250-02 is the lowest-grade stope (4.1 g/t) among those that load only. Under LOADER-BACKUP-02, stopes in a combined cycle can't give up their loader.
- **Net result:** about 187.5 t (50.64 oz) is protected at TP-1310-04. TP-1250-02 loses about 145 t (19.11 oz), so the net protected is 31.53 oz.
- **Options compared (shift loss in total):**

| Option | Tonnes lost | Ounces lost |
|---|---|---|
| Do nothing | 231 | 62.39 |
| Wait for repair (back about 14:30) | 156 | 42.13 |
| Reassign LH-11 | 188.5 | 30.86 |

- **Confidence:** 0.55. The 09:45 start is my assumption. The repair estimate is only a crew guess because the CMMS has been down since 09:00. I listed who to ask for the missing information in the proposal.
